Supplied built-Gateway comparisons reproduce excluded history returning on main and disappearing on the candidate through actual isolated finalization; this review executed no target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The smallest complete repair transports the existing frozen selected view to history preparation, preserving its bounds and transcript custody without restoring the live engine or introducing a second context owner. Thanks @ericcaiwx-star for picking up #186244. We had started on the same defect and stopped once we saw this draft, so this is yours. A few findings from our source audit that may save you a round:

- Forwarding the selected context engine into the whole isolated finalizer is not safe as-is. The second attempt would then run engine bootstrap/maintenance (`attempt-session-prepare.ts`), install the mid-loop ingestion/afterTurn hook (`attempt-setup.ts`, `tool-result-context-guard.ts`), and repeat terminal ingestion/afterTurn/maintenance (`attempt-finalize.ts`). Reusing the already engine-assembled settled snapshot through the existing history-preparation owner, as this PR proposes, avoids all of that. If you do assemble fresh instead, keep the engine out of the finalizer lifecycle and expose it only at assembly, and skip ambient memory prompt preparation and engine system additions.
- The exact current-turn split is already recorded by the prompt owner (`attempt-prompt-build.ts`) and carried with the settled model snapshot. Please don't infer it from the last user text or a tool-call ID. Compaction can invalidate that count; the usage-snapshot owner already treats it as unreliable after compaction, so the finalizer should too. Empty-finalizer retries should reuse the original bounded view rather than re-reading raw history.
- A useful proof shape: a minimal synthetic context-engine plugin that keeps long raw history but assembles only one short summary plus the current settled receipts, a recording OpenAI-compatible provider that returns a harmless read and then an empty final (forcing isolated finalization), and lifecycle counters for assemble/bootstrap/maintain/ingest/afterTurn. Base should leak old canary text into the finalization request; the fix should send the bounded summary plus the current receipt, offer zero tools, and leave the lifecycle counters unchanged. Note that a plain read-only flow often ends in an ordinary tool-enabled continuation and never reaches isolated finalization, so check that the captured request really is the finalizer before drawing conclusions.

The already-delivered-message admission question in the issue is tracked separately in #179003 and doesn't need to be solved here.

## Independent current-main Gateway proof

Rechecked against main `4b27ee88cec9a78377a04b2e3a352ba7c503450e` and PR production code at `f616ee3a246c95c0d44521687495ab828a880516`. The contributor's new head `a037f29b1bad9717aca3a3db9559b941534e4efd` changes only the two existing test files; those latest tests were adopted and validated separately.

The experiment used built Gateways in secretless Linux/Node 24.22.1 isolation, real `sessions.create`, `chat.send`, and `agent.wait` RPCs, a selected synthetic context engine, and a recording local Chat Completions SSE provider. Each session first saved about 48 KB of synthetic raw canary history. The next turn performed a real `write` to a task-owned workspace file and received an empty post-tool answer, forcing the isolated finalizer. Using a write is intentional: a plain read can admit an ordinary tool-enabled continuation instead.

| Case | Finalizer request JSON bytes | Old raw canary | Selected summary | Current write receipt | Offered tools |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| Main, run 1 | 52,100 | present | absent | present | 0 |
| Main, run 2 | 52,100 | present | absent | present | 0 |
| Candidate, run 1 | 2,505 | absent | present | present | 0 |
| Candidate, run 2 | 2,505 | absent | present | present | 0 |

Both source requests excluded the old canary before finalization. Lifecycle records were unchanged between each settled tool-result request and its actual isolated-finalizer request: no extra bootstrap, maintenance, assemble, ingestion, afterTurn, or commitTurn calls. Auxiliary activity-summary requests were distinguished from finalizers by their system-role metadata prompt and were not counted in the table.

Normal-finalization controls on both revisions returned a visible answer directly after the write, retained the selected summary/current receipt, omitted the old canary, and never entered isolated finalization. All six measured turns completed with `agent.wait` status `ok`; each retained the two real user inputs and the answer in `chat.history`.

Maintainer audit points: the fix transports the frozen settled view, not the live engine; it adds no heuristic current-turn split or assembly lifecycle; the existing history owner applies its normal byte/event and tool-result bounds. The detached regression covers reusing the original view across an empty finalizer retry. Compaction remains under the existing snapshot/capture owner's rules. Already-delivered-message admission (#179003) stays out of scope.

Latest contributor head passed the two changed suites (11 tests across two routed shards), focused Oxlint, and Oxfmt in isolation. The retained selected-view regression failed on main because excluded history reappeared. Whole-PR delta: production +65/-5 (net +60), tests +104/-104 (net 0); no ceiling or baseline changed. The contributor independently supplied the same test-line repair while this experiment was running, so no redundant cleanup commit was added.

These are measured HTTP request bytes, not real-provider token usage or billing. Fixtures are synthetic; no live channel, OAuth, or third-party context-engine deployment claim is made.
